blocks.html: El 25 Fishing Guide — San Jose del Cabo
Discover El 25 fishing near San Jose del Cabo: yellowfin tuna, wahoo, dorado, jigging and bottom fishing with private charters from Puerto Los Cabos.

El 25 is a versatile fishing ground near San Jose del Cabo, with documented opportunities for yellowfin tuna, wahoo, dorado and bottom-dwelling species. Its appeal lies in the ability to explore different fishing techniques and nearby structures as conditions change.

Regional fishing reports frequently mention El 25 alongside Iman Bank, La Fortuna and other northeastern Sea of Cortez fishing grounds.

Although the area has produced good fishing on particular days, catches can vary substantially between reporting periods.

Where Is El 25 Fishing Ground?

El 25 is one of the recognized fishing locations northeast of Puerto Los Cabos Marina.

It forms part of a wider network of underwater fishing structures explored by anglers departing from San Jose del Cabo.

Regional reports often refer to this area simply as “25.”

Depending on bait availability, current, wind and fish activity, a fishing outing may focus on El 25 or move between adjacent grounds.

Because conditions can change quickly, selecting one location in advance does not guarantee it will be the most productive choice.

What Fish Can You Catch at El 25?

Yellowfin Tuna — Documented Spring Activity

Yellowfin tuna are among the species reported around El 25.

During the week ending March 22, 2026, regional fishing reports described smaller tuna in the 10–20-pound range around Iman and El 25.

Earlier that week, El 25 produced some of the better small-tuna action, with several outings reporting multiple yellowfin caught on live or dead sardines.

A separate report from March 8, 2026, also documented small tuna activity at El 25 later in the morning.

These observations demonstrate that the area can offer yellowfin tuna opportunities, but they do not establish a dependable daily bite.

Larger yellowfin tuna are also encountered in the broader San Jose del Cabo fishing region. Their reported presence elsewhere should not be presented as an El 25 catch.

Wahoo — Trolling the Fishing Grounds

Wahoo are another important species associated with El 25.

In September 2025, a regional report described wahoo activity across La Fortuna, El 25 and Iman Bank.

Reported fish averaged approximately 25 pounds, with some in the 40–45-pound range.

Deep-diving trolling lures produced many of the strikes in that wider area.

Wahoo activity was again reported around La Fortuna, El 25 and Cardon in January 2026.

These examples show that El 25 can be part of a productive trolling route when regional reports indicate wahoo are present.

Dorado — An Additional Pelagic Opportunity

Dorado are documented around El 25 and nearby fishing grounds.

The March 29, 2026, regional report described dorado weighing approximately 25–40 pounds across Iman, El 25, La Fortuna and Inner Gordo.

Live bait was used for some catches, while trolling remained an option for anglers covering a wider area.

Dorado may be encountered while targeting other pelagic species, but their presence and feeding activity are highly variable.

Snapper, Grouper and Amberjack

El 25 is also included in regional reports covering fishing on rocky bottom structure.

Historical observations from September 2025 and March 2026 describe mixed catches of snapper, grouper and amberjack across El 25 and neighboring fishing grounds.

These species may respond to chunks of bait or vertical jigs when conditions permit.

Currents can make it difficult to keep a jig or bait close to the intended structure, so bottom fishing is not always the most effective option.

Fishing Techniques at El 25

Several techniques are documented across this fishing area:

  • Live or dead sardines: For yellowfin tuna.

  • Strips of squid: Another bait used for tuna in the surrounding grounds.

  • Deep-diving trolling lures: Particularly for wahoo.

  • Rigged ballyhoo: Used while covering water for pelagic species.

  • Vertical jigging: For bottom-associated fish and baitfish.

  • Drifting cut bait: For snapper, grouper and other species near rocky structure.

A flexible plan allows anglers to respond to what is happening on the water rather than relying on a single fishing method.

How Does El 25 Compare With Other Fishing Grounds?

One advantage of considering El 25 is its proximity within the broader group of northeastern San Jose del Cabo fishing locations.

La Fortuna has regional reports involving wahoo, dorado and mixed fishing opportunities.

Iman Bank is frequently mentioned for yellowfin tuna and bottom fishing.

San Luis offers bottom structure as well as nearby coastal fishing opportunities.

El 25 can be one option within a broader fishing plan, particularly when reports indicate fish moving between neighboring grounds.

What Time of Year Is Best for El 25?

Historical reports document activity in January, March and September, involving different species.

However, those examples do not mean every January, March or September will produce the same results.

Ocean conditions, available bait, wind and current can all influence fishing success.

For practical trip planning, recent regional observations are more useful than treating one historical month as a guaranteed season.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is El 25 good for yellowfin tuna?

Yellowfin tuna have been documented at El 25, including smaller fish during March 2026. The fishing can be inconsistent.

Are wahoo caught around El 25?

Yes. Regional reports include wahoo activity at El 25 and neighboring grounds, particularly when trolling diving lures.

Is El 25 only for offshore trolling?

No. Reports also describe fishing over rocky bottom structures, including opportunities for snapper, grouper and amberjack.
